title: The live canary sends a custom provider's resolved compat configuration and nothing credential-bearing
statement: For a custom provider whose `models.json` declares `compat`, the live canary's child receives the `compat` configuration Pi resolves for the selected model. Measured against a local loopback provider: the request observed at the provider matches the request that configuration produces, and the compatibility record written from that run matches the same configuration. Controls: (1) changing `compat` after a passed canary makes the stored record fail to prove the next launch; (2) the configuration passed to the child is closed, and anything outside it is refused before any child is created. It has no `apiKey`, `headers` or `authHeader` at the provider or model level, and no key named for a credential at any depth. A string value may appear only in the provider's `baseUrl` (with no user, password, query or fragment) and `api`; in each model's `id`, `name` and `input` modalities; in compat fields whose values Pi restricts to fixed literals, and only as one of those literals; and as a chat-template variable's `$var`. Elsewhere, including `samplingParams`, chat-template arguments and structured routing fields, values are numbers, booleans or null. A model whose request needs any other value cannot be proved by the live check. (3) The child's `models.json` is checked byte for byte. Its only credential field is the provider's `apiKey`, which the canary writes as exactly `$NAME` of the declared variable, and it contains no credential value, no header and no other credential field.
notes: Evidence recorded 2026-09-24 in EVD-0147, and left not-evaluated for review. The control passed in all four cells of CI run 36077139114. In the earlier red run 36076748293 it failed once on Windows Node 22, at its launch step, from F130 mechanism 2, after its compat assertions had passed. ⚠️ STATEMENT AMENDED 2026-09-25 on review. Control (2) had said the child's file contains no `apiKey`, but the canary intentionally writes the provider's `apiKey` as `$NAME`; that exception is now stated and tested on the file's bytes. Refusing credential-NAMED keys could not show that a value under an innocuous key is non-secret, so the accepted values are now a closed contract, and any string outside it is refused. Stays not-evaluated for review. ⚠️ PASS 2026-09-25 on EVD-0147, on review. The amended contract, the child-file byte check and the real-command control passed in all four cells of CI run 36122196186 at cacb817. That run was RED OVERALL: ACC-0116 failed on Windows Node 22 with Not observed: agent-descendants (F130 mechanism 2), which is unrelated to this criterion.
